title: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability incident followup

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-24 15:30 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Sofia Chen, Marcus Patel - Redwood; Daniel Ruiz, Priya Shah, Karen Li, Tom Evans - Aperture Financial

Summary: quick run through of last week's reliability incident (spike of 5xxs + timeouts during peak batch run). Goal: identify immediate mitigations, and map longer-term options (dedicated vs hosted).

Topics: incident timeline, logs, retries, rate limits, caching, monitoring/alerts, next steps.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to start with a quick recap of the incident on Sunday where you saw a spike in 5xxs and a bunch of client timeouts. Marcus is here to walk through the telemetry we pulled.
[00:22] Marcus (Redwood SE): Hi all. Quick note - I pulled the logs from the window 03-21 18:00 to 03-21 19:30 UTC. We see a burst of errors roughly 18:12 to 18:28, mostly 502/503s, plus a few client-side 504s. Some of those 504s appear to be timeouts on your side due to waiting for retries.
[00:38] Daniel (DevOps): Yeah that matches our timeline. We had a nightly re-rate job that kicked off at 18:10 which sent a lot of concurrent requests. We normally throttle but this run was higher.
[00:50] Priya (ML Eng): Fwiw we also saw increased token lengths on some requests - a couple of large prompt reruns which increased prediction time. Could be compounding.
[01:05] Tom (SRE): Quick question - are the 5xxs coming from Redwood runtime or from our gateway? The traces are a bit noisy.
[01:15] Marcus: Most of the 5xxs are from the inference tier - our front proxy returned 502/503 when the model worker couldn't service an incoming request within the worker-side timeout. There are two things in play: sudden concurrency + a few long running requests that pinned resources.
[01:31] Karen (Product): So is this a capacity issue or a software bug? We need to know for our exec update.
[01:40] Sofia: Short answer: capacity + workload pattern. Not a silent bug, more a mismatch between request patterns and current pool sizing + caching config.
[01:49] Daniel: We'd like to avoid shared-hosted throttling if possible - our data sensitivity team prefers dedicated. But cost is a factor.
[01:57] Marcus: Right, dedicated capacity would give you predictable throughput. But there are short-term mitigations we can do while you evaluate - e.g., client-side rate limiting, prefixed requests, and better retry/backoff.
[02:12] Priya: About retries - currently our SDK retries quickly, like linear backoff at 200ms increments, up to 3 retries. That might be exacerbating the pressure.
[02:23] Marcus: Exactly. We recommend switching to exponential backoff with jitter, and also respect Retry-After headers. Example: initial backoff 250ms, multiplier 2, jitter 0.2 up to a max of 5s and cap total attempts. We'll draft a sample patch.
[02:40] Tom: Also our gateway sets a per-request timeout of 15s - is that aligned with Redwood's worker timeout? We saw some 504s where the gateway gave up earlier.
[02:52] Marcus: Our worker timeouts default to 30s on the hosted pool for large models. If your gateway times out earlier, clients will surface 504 and start retrying. So alignment is important.
[03:06] Daniel: Ok, so one immediate step is to increase our gateway timeout to 35s during peak runs and implement smarter retries.
[03:16] Sofia: Also we noticed a lot of repeated prefixes - enabling prefix KV caching could reduce worker load for repeated contexts. It requires a small model config tweak; Marcus can share recommended settings.
[03:29] Priya: Is KV cache the same as the K-V cash Marcus? Sorry, transcription - I keep getting mixed up.
[03:36] Marcus: (laughs) K-V cache, yep - key-value cache. It helps if you have repeated conversation prefixes or large shared prompt fragments.
[03:44] Karen: For the POC success criteria, can we define an acceptable error rate? Last week we saw a 2.8% 5xx rate during that window which felt high. What's reasonable?
[03:55] Marcus: For production SLAs we aim <0.1% 5xx over a 24h window, but for POC pilot you're commonly at a higher baseline. We can aim for <0.5% in steady-state for the pilot before scaling.
[04:07] Daniel: And what about rate limits - we hit 429s too. Were those Redwood-enforced or our gateway?
[04:15] Marcus: The 429s were gateway-side throttles from your IP layer; we also returned 429s once our quota markers were hit on the hosted pool. We can add soft throttling and better headers so your clients can detect and back off early.
[04:31] Priya: Can you send us a list of headers and example Retry-After behavior we should expect?
[04:36] Sofia: Yes, we'll attach a short spec including which headers we set, sample values, and recommended client behavior.
[04:44] Daniel: Regarding logs - can you provide sanitized request/trace ids? We want to correlate with our side.
[04:51] Marcus: We'll share a filtered slice (no PII) of traces and stack traces for the time window. Should come through by EOD tomorrow.
[04:58] Karen: For the medium-term, can you size a dedicated pool for our peak? We had about 1200 concurrent requests during a 15-minute spike.
[05:09] Marcus: We'll run a sizing exercise: need model type, typical prompt sizes, and token output distributions. If you can share those numbers we can recommend GPU count and burst capacity.
[05:22] Priya: I'll pull token distribution histograms and send. Also, note that a few requests hit our max prompt length; we may trim some early.
[05:31] Sofia: Helpful - that will inform kernel selection and batching strategies too.
[05:38] Tom: On monitoring - can we get a per-route dashboard that shows retry rates, 5xxs, median latency and p99?
[05:47] Marcus: Yes, Redwood Console can emit per-route dashboards and alerting. We can provision a dashboard for Aperture and add alert rules for >0.5% 5xxs over 10m or sustained p95 latency increase.
[06:01] Daniel: Great. Also, we want better observability on backoff-induced delay so we don't misinterpret retries as new traffic.
[06:08] Marcus: We'll include tracing tags to indicate retries vs original request and include a unique client attempt id in traces.
[06:16] Karen: Slight aside - security team asked about audit logs and KMS for any dedicated deployment. Can you confirm KMS options?
[06:25] Sofia: Yes, for Private or Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS/HSM integrations; we'll attach the security doc.
[06:33] Daniel: Perfect - send that.
[06:36] Priya: Any quick wins we can roll out overnight?
[06:40] Marcus: Immediate wins: (1) change client retry to exponential with jitter, (2) increase gateway timeout to match worker timeout, (3) enable prefix KV caching on repeat-heavy routes, (4) soft-concurrency limits on client side during batch jobs. These should reduce pressure tonight.
[06:57] Sofia: We'll also temporarily bump your hosted pool burst capacity by 10% to help the next scheduled run while we evaluate dedicated sizing.
[07:06] Daniel: Appreciate that. One more question: in case of future 5xx spikes, what's your recommended incident playbook?
[07:13] Marcus: Short playbook: 1) detect via alert (we'll configure), 2) throttle clients via token bucket or soft-limit, 3) increase worker count or route to fallback model variant, 4) engage SE/AE and open a bridge. We'll document this and share an incident runbook.
[07:31] Karen: Ok, let's recap next steps.
[07:35] Sofia: Recap - Redwood to share sanitized traces and header spec by EOD tomorrow; Marcus to send recommended retry/backoff patch and KV cache config by Thu; Aperture to run synthetic multi-region load test and share results by 2026-03-30; schedule deep-dive next week for capacity sizing.
[07:52] Daniel: Sounds good. We'll confirm a time for the deep-dive. Thanks team.
[07:57] Sofia: Thanks all - closing notes: I'll drop the action items into the CRM and share links to the docs.
[08:05] Priya: Thanks, bye.

--- End transcript ---

References/links mentioned: Redwood Console dashboard (link shared in chat), sanitized-traces.zip (to be shared), retry-sample.patch.diff (to be shared).
